standard_prerequisites.name: Finite presentation of a module relative to a base ring
standard_prerequisites.use: Fixes the meaning of the hypothesis: an explicit presentation over a polynomial ring over R rather than over A.

standard_prerequisites.name: Base change of modules and of polynomial algebras along a ring map
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the presentation over R'[x_1, ..., x_n] from the presentation over R[x_1, ..., x_n] and identifies M tensor_A A' with M tensor_R R'.

core_obligations: Choose a surjection R[x_1, ..., x_n] -> A, which is possible because R -> A is of finite type (proof line 21059).
Choose a presentation R[x_1, ..., x_n]^{oplus s} -> R[x_1, ..., x_n]^{oplus t} -> M -> 0 witnessing that M is finitely presented relative to R (proof lines 21060-21063).
Apply the functor - tensor_R R' to that presentation to obtain R'[x_1, ..., x_n]^{oplus s} -> R'[x_1, ..., x_n]^{oplus t} -> M tensor_R R' -> 0 (proof lines 21064-21068).
Conclude that the resulting sequence is a presentation of the base change, so M tensor_A A' is finitely presented relative to R' (proof line 21069).
difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a finite type ring map R -> A, an A-module M finitely presented relative to R, and an arbitrary ring map R -> R', and asserts that M tensor_A A' = M tensor_R R' is finitely presented relative to R' (source lines 21047-21056). The proof must convert relative finite presentation into an explicit two-step free presentation over the polynomial ring R[x_1, ..., x_n] after choosing a surjection R[x_1, ..., x_n] -> A (proof lines 21058-21063), and then push that presentation along R -> R' to obtain a presentation of the base change over R'[x_1, ..., x_n] (proof lines 21064-21069). The step that is not purely formal is recognising that base change of the chosen presentation is again a presentation, which the author records by the word 'we win' rather than by an argument.
